placement_modes.rationale: Follows the DrivAerML relative-diagnostics contract: every diagnostic kind is published in a constant-placement family and a geometry-following relative family, linked by source_family_id. The constant family is scored; the relative family is report-only at zero weight until it is reviewed.
placement_modes.why_windsorml_only_needs_a_vertical_rela: Streamwise and lateral extents are identical in all 350 published runs (nose x = -0.56075, base x = 0.48325, half width 0.1945), so a constant x or z station is already the same physical location in every case. Only body HEIGHT varies, from 0.29957 m to 0.48888 m across the scored cases. The relative frame therefore rescales the vertical coordinate alone, which is a much smaller change than DrivAerML's, where wheelhouses and body length also move.
placement_modes.why_both_are_needed: A constant station at y = 0.194 m is 65% of the shortest scored body's height but 40% of the tallest, so it samples a different part of the roof shear layer per case and the metric partly measures geometry rather than flow prediction. A relative station at fixed y/h samples the same position in the shear layer for every case, but is no longer a fixed physical probe location. Neither alone is sufficient, which is why both are published.

relative_frame.h_case_definition: the maximum y of that case's native boundary mesh, i.e. the body top above the ground plane at y = 0
relative_frame.h_case_source: measured per case during profile-support generation and recorded in the per-case support file
relative_frame.anchoring: Relative eta values are chosen so that each relative station reduces exactly to its constant counterpart on the reference case run_0. That makes the two families directly comparable there and gives the relative family a verifiable equivalence check.

provenance.why: AutoCFD Case 1 is the same 1/4-scale Windsor body and shares this dataset's reference area of 0.112 m^2. Measured geometry matches the published meshes exactly: length 1044 mm, width 389 mm.
provenance.axis_note: AutoCFD reports 2D PIV on planes y = 0 mm and z = 194 mm. Under its SAE convention (x rearward, y lateral, z up) those are the symmetry plane and a horizontal plane 194 mm above the ground, mapping to z = 0 and y = 0.194 m in WindsorML's mirrored frame.
provenance.axis_caveat: The AutoCFD public case page does not state its coordinate origin, so the mapping is inferred from plane semantics. It is not load-bearing: y = 0.194 m lies inside the body for every published variant.

geometry_invariants.body_height_range_source: measured over all 233 scored cases during profile-support generation; shortest run_8, tallest run_264

resolution_evidence.method: run_0 velocity profiles regenerated at 64/96/128/160 samples, resampled onto the 64-sample grid, compared as max |delta ux/uinf|
resolution_evidence.interpretation: Differences between sample counts are at most about 2% of U_inf and are NOT monotonic. This is zeroth-order cell quantisation, not unresolved profile structure and not a nearest-centre artefact: each sample takes the constant value of the cell containing it, so different sample counts land in different cells. 128 samples over a 0.6 m line is 4.7 mm spacing against 3-8 mm cells, so sampling already sits at the mesh scale and higher counts resample the same cells.
resolution_evidence.residual_noise_note: The resulting 1-2% of U_inf quantisation floor is inherent to sampling a finite-volume CellData field at points, and DrivAerML and AhmedML carry the same floor by design. Interpolating cell-centred data would invent information that the discretisation does not contain, so it is deliberately not done. HiLiftAeroML interpolates only because its surface fields are nodal and therefore genuinely piecewise-linear.

velocity_stations.reference_velocity_source: measured far-field velocityxavg at x > base + 1.5 m, y > 1.5 * body height, |z| < 0.05 m

pressure_stations.selection_note: Surface stations resolve to the nearest native boundary POINT, because WindsorML publishes cpavg on points. Each station is a well-defined curve on the closed body, not an arbitrary plane intersection.

constant.label: Upper centreline, nose to base
constant.rule: for each sampled x, the largest-y boundary point with |z| < 0.004 m
constant.note: Follows the body surface by construction, so it is identical in the relative family apart from its parameterisation.

constant.label: Base vertical centreline
constant.rule: for each sampled y, the boundary point nearest (base_x, y, 0) with |z| < 0.004 m and x > base_x - 0.01
constant.note: The canonical Windsor base-pressure line. The constant interval overshoots short bodies, which is exactly what the relative counterpart fixes.

constant.label: Side surface, horizontal cut at y = 194 mm
constant.rule: for each sampled x, the largest-z boundary point with |y - 0.194| < 0.004 m

relative.rule: identical selection, parameterised by x/L rather than x
for each sampled eta, the boundary point nearest (base_x, eta * h_case, 0)
relative.note: Spans exactly the base from ground to body top in every case, instead of a fixed 0.5 m that over- or under-runs it.

relative.rule: for each sampled x, the largest-z boundary point with |y - eta * h_case| < 0.004 m, eta = 0.56491
relative.note: eta = 0.56491 reproduces y = 0.194 m exactly on run_0 (h = 0.34342 m).

volume.implementation: KD-tree candidates over cell centres inside the station box, then exact vtkGenericCell.EvaluatePosition; ties take the smallest raw cell ID; a sample with no containing cell falls back to the nearest centre and is counted
volume.matches: DrivAerML (vtkCellTreeLocator + EvaluatePosition) and AhmedML (vtkStaticCellLocator.FindCell with counted fallback)
volume.polyhedron_note: WindsorML volumes are 100% hexahedra (291,324,855 of 291,324,855 in run_0), so DrivAerML's deterministic polyhedron kernel -- which exists because vtkPolyhedron::IsInside in VTK 9.5.2 seeds a private random sequence from wall-clock time -- is not needed here.
volume.ground_plane_fallbacks: Vertical stations begin at y = 0, which lies on the ground plane outside the fluid mesh, so each contributes exactly one counted fallback. The lateral station, at y = 0.194 m, has none.

surface.implementation: each sample selects an actual native boundary point by a geometric rule (for example the largest-y point in a thin centreline slab), rather than sampling an arbitrary location
surface.matches: DrivAerML cp, whose exported truth declares zeroth-order native values with no interpolation, snapping, remeshing, or gap filling
surface.note: Because the curve is made of native entities, surface profiles carry no sampling error at all. Interpolation would be legitimate here -- cpavg is nodal, as in HiLiftAeroML -- but is unnecessary while the stations select points directly.

kernel_change_evidence.wall_time_cost: 639 s versus 637 s per case; the volume read dominates and the point queries are negligible
kernel_change_evidence.interpretation: On a Cartesian hexahedral mesh the nearest cell centre is almost always the containing cell, so the two kernels nearly agree. Containing-cell is still adopted because it is exact, matches the sibling datasets, and makes the ground-plane samples explicit instead of silently snapping them.
